claim: Floral transition involves changes in shape and identity of the shoot apical meristem (SAM).
source: Floral transition, the onset of plant reproduction, involves changes in shape and identity of the shoot apical meristem (SAM).
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the biological process under study.

claim: The change in SAM shape during floral transition is termed doming.
source: The change in shape, termed doming, occurs early during floral transition when it is induced by environmental cues such as changes in day-length, but how it is regulated at the cellular level is unknown.
evidence: The abstract explicitly defines the morphological change as 'doming'.

claim: Both cell number and size increased during doming of the SAM.
source: Both cell number and size increased during doming, and these changes were partially controlled by the gene regulatory network (GRN) that triggers flowering.
evidence: The abstract states this as a finding from the study.

claim: Changes in cell number and size during doming were partially controlled by the gene regulatory network that triggers flowering.
source: Both cell number and size increased during doming, and these changes were partially controlled by the gene regulatory network (GRN) that triggers flowering.
evidence: The abstract presents this as a conclusion from experimental data.

claim: Dynamic modulation of expression of gibberellin biosynthesis and catabolism enzymes at the SAM contributed to doming.
source: Furthermore, dynamic modulation of expression of gibberellin (GA) biosynthesis and catabolism enzymes at the SAM contributed to doming.
evidence: The abstract states this as a finding from the study.

claim: Expression of GA biosynthesis and catabolism enzymes was regulated by two MADS-domain transcription factors implicated in flowering.
source: Expression of these enzymes was regulated by two MADS-domain transcription factors implicated in flowering.
evidence: The abstract presents this as a finding from the study.

claim: In Arabidopsis thaliana, leaf primordia are formed during vegetative growth.
source: In the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana, leaf primordia are formed during vegetative growth, but at floral transition the developmental identity of the SAM changes to an inflorescence meristem, and it initiates the formation of floral primordia.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Arabidopsis development.

claim: At floral transition, the developmental identity of the SAM changes to an inflorescence meristem.
source: In the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana, leaf primordia are formed during vegetative growth, but at floral transition the developmental identity of the SAM changes to an inflorescence meristem, and it initiates the formation of floral primordia.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Arabidopsis development.

claim: Floral induction of A. thaliana occurs rapidly in response to exposure to long days.
source: For example, floral induction of A. thaliana occurs rapidly in response to exposure to long days (LDs).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Arabidopsis photoperiodic response, with a citation to Andrés and Coupland, 2012.

claim: The SAM is considered to consist of three regions: the central zone (CZ), the peripheral zone (PZ), and the rib zone (RZ).
source: The SAM is considered to consist of three regions based on histological and functional analyses: the central zone (CZ), the peripheral zone (PZ), and the rib zone (RZ) (Barton, 2010; Bowman and Eshed, 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to previous work.

claim: The CZ contains the stem cells.
source: The CZ contains the stem cells, the PZ gives rise to primordia, and the RZ forms the stem.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about SAM organization.

claim: Cells in the CZ divide slowly.
source: Cells in the CZ divide slowly, whereas cells in the PZ divide more frequently to produce organ primordia.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about cell division patterns in the SAM.

claim: Cells in the PZ divide more frequently to produce organ primordia.
source: Cells in the CZ divide slowly, whereas cells in the PZ divide more frequently to produce organ primordia.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about cell division patterns in the SAM.

claim: Mitotic activity in the SAM of A. thaliana increased in both the CZ and the PZ during floral induction initiated by exposure to LDs.
source: During floral induction initiated by exposure to LDs, mitotic activity in the SAM of A. thaliana was measured by tritiated thymidine labeling and was found to increase in both the CZ and the PZ (Jacqmard et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from a previous study with citation.

claim: FT and TSF are paralogous proteins that represent the output of the photoperiodic flowering pathway.
source: The paralogous proteins FLOWERING LOCUS T (FT) and TWIN SISTER OF FT (TSF) represent the output of this pathway (Kardailsky et al., 1999; Kobayashi et al., 1999; Yamaguchi et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to previous work.

claim: FT and TSF are transcribed specifically under LDs in the leaf vasculature.
source: FT and TSF are transcribed specifically under LDs in the leaf vasculature, and the FT protein is transported to the SAM, where it interacts with 14-3-3 proteins and a bZIP transcription factor, FD, to promote the transcription of floral integrator genes (Abe et al., 2005; Abe et al., 2019; Collani et al., 2019; Corbesier et al., 2007; Jaeger and Wigge, 2007; Mathieu et al., 2007; Romera-Branchat et al., 2020; Tamaki et al., 2007; Taoka et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with multiple citations.

claim: The FT protein is transported to the SAM.
source: FT and TSF are transcribed specifically under LDs in the leaf vasculature, and the FT protein is transported to the SAM, where it interacts with 14-3-3 proteins and a bZIP transcription factor, FD, to promote the transcription of floral integrator genes (Abe et al., 2005; Abe et al., 2019; Collani et al., 2019; Corbesier et al., 2007; Jaeger and Wigge, 2007; Mathieu et al., 2007; Romera-Branchat et al., 2020; Tamaki et al., 2007; Taoka et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with multiple citations.

claim: FT interacts with 14-3-3 proteins and FD to promote the transcription of floral integrator genes.
source: FT and TSF are transcribed specifically under LDs in the leaf vasculature, and the FT protein is transported to the SAM, where it interacts with 14-3-3 proteins and a bZIP transcription factor, FD, to promote the transcription of floral integrator genes (Abe et al., 2005; Abe et al., 2019; Collani et al., 2019; Corbesier et al., 2007; Jaeger and Wigge, 2007; Mathieu et al., 2007; Romera-Branchat et al., 2020; Tamaki et al., 2007; Taoka et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with multiple citations.

claim: SOC1 is the earliest known gene to respond directly to FT/FD at the SAM.
source: The earliest known gene to respond directly to FT/FD at the SAM is SUPPRESSOR OF OVEREXPRESSION OF CONSTANS 1 (SOC1) that encodes a MADS-domain type transcription factor (Lee et al., 2000; Samach et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The FT/FD complex activates the transcription of APETALA1 (AP1).
source: Subsequently, the FT/FD complex also activates the transcription of APETALA1 (AP1), another gene encoding a MADS-domain transcription factor that confers floral identity on primordia on the flanks of the SAM (Abe et al., 2005; Collani et al., 2019; Wigge et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: AP1 confers floral identity on primordia on the flanks of the SAM.
source: Subsequently, the FT/FD complex also activates the transcription of APETALA1 (AP1), another gene encoding a MADS-domain transcription factor that confers floral identity on primordia on the flanks of the SAM (Abe et al., 2005; Collani et al., 2019; Wigge et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: SVP inhibits flowering by reducing transcription of FT, TSF, and SOC1.
source: On the other hand, flowering of A. thaliana is severely delayed under non-inductive short-day conditions, in which the MADS-domain transcription factor SHORT VEGETATIVE PHASE (SVP) inhibits flowering by reducing transcription of FT, TSF, and SOC1 (Hartmann et al., 2000; Jang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The SAM of Col-0 plants grown for 2 weeks under SDs becomes committed to floral induction around 5 days after transfer to LDs.
source: The onset of flowering can be synchronized by transferring plants from SDs to LDs, and in the wild-type accession Col-0, the SAM of plants grown for 2 weeks under SDs becomes committed to floral induction around 5 days after transfer to LDs (Torti et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: GA promotes diverse biological processes, including cell elongation, cell division, and floral induction.
source: GA promotes diverse biological processes, including cell elongation, cell division, and floral induction (Yamaguchi, 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: The ga1-3 mutant of A. thaliana is late flowering under LDs and fails to flower under SDs.
source: The strongly GA-deficient ga1-3 mutant of A. thaliana is late flowering under LDs and fails to flower under SDs (Wilson et al., 1992).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: The level of bioactive GA4 increases strongly in shoot apices under SDs around the time of floral induction.
source: Corresponding to this phenotype, the level of bioactive GA4 increases strongly in shoot apices under SDs around the time of floral induction (Eriksson et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Local GA biosynthesis is largely dependent on the activity of GA20-oxidase (GA20ox) and GA3-oxidase (GA3ox) enzymes.
source: Local GA biosynthesis is largely dependent on the activity of the 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase (2ODD) enzymes GA20-oxidase (GA20ox) and GA3-oxidase (GA3ox) that convert the GA precursor GA12 into bioactive GA4 (Yamaguchi, 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: GA2-oxidase (GA2ox) contributes to the inactivation of GA4 or its precursors.
source: By contrast, the 2ODD enzyme GA2-oxidase (GA2ox) contributes to the inactivation of GA4 or its precursors and regulates the concentration of bioactive GA in vivo (Yamaguchi, 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Bioactive GA is perceived by its receptor, GIBBERELLIN INSENSITIVE DWARF1 (GID1).
source: Bioactive GA is perceived by its receptor, GIBBERELLIN INSENSITIVE DWARF1 (GID1) (Griffiths et al., 2006; Willige et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The GID1–GA complex interacts directly with DELLA proteins and induces their degradation by the 26S-proteasome pathway.
source: The GID1–GA complex interacts directly with DELLA proteins and induces their degradation by the 26S-proteasome pathway through the E3 ubiquitin ligase SLEEPY (SLY) and SNEEZY (SNE) (Ariizumi et al., 2011; Griffiths et al., 2006; McGinnis et al., 2003; Willige et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: DELLA proteins are repressors of GA-mediated growth and development.
source: DELLA proteins are repressors of GA-mediated growth and development, and they interact with a broad range of transcription factors to alter their DNA binding properties or transcriptional activity (Marín-de la Rosa et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: In A. thaliana there are five DELLA proteins, of which RGA and GAI are major repressors of growth and reproductive development.
source: In A. thaliana there are five DELLA proteins, of which REPRESSOR OF ga1-3 (RGA) and GA INSENSITIVE (GAI) are major repressors of growth and reproductive development (Dill and Sun, 2001; Peng et al., 1997; Silverstone et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: GA levels are strongly repressed in the SAM of different plant species during vegetative development.
source: GA levels are strongly repressed in the SAM of different plant species during vegetative development.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: KNOX transcription factors are expressed in the SAM from the early stages of embryogenesis.
source: Establishment and maintenance of the SAM involve KNOTTED1-LIKE homeobox (KNOX) transcription factors, such as KNOTTED1 (KN1) in maize and SHOOTMERISTEMLESS (STM) in A. thaliana, which are expressed in the SAM from the early stages of embryogenesis (Bowman and Eshed, 2000; Long et al., 1996; Vollbrecht et al., 1991).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: A major function of KNOX transcription factors is the reduction in GA levels in the SAM.
source: A major function of KNOX transcription factors is the reduction in GA levels in the SAM (Bolduc and Hake, 2009; Hay et al., 2002; Jasinski et al., 2005; Sakamoto et al., 2001a; Sakamoto et al., 2001b).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: In maize, KN1 directly binds to and activates expression of the GA2ox1 gene.
source: In maize, KN1 directly binds to and activates expression of the GA2ox1 gene that encodes a GA catabolic enzyme.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: In Arabidopsis and tobacco, the activity of STM and its homologue NTH15 are associated with reduced expression of GA20ox genes.
source: Similarly, in Arabidopsis and tobacco, the activity of STM and its homologue NTH15, respectively, are associated with reduced expression of GA20ox genes that encode GA biosynthetic enzymes (Hay et al., 2002; Jasinski et al., 2005; Sakamoto et al., 2001a).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The area of the SAM and the distance between primordia on opposite sides of the SAM gradually increased between 2wSD and 3wSD in wild-type plants grown in non-inductive SDs.
source: In wild-type plants grown in non-inductive SDs, the area of the SAM and the distance between primordia on opposite sides of the SAM gradually increased between 2wSD and 3wSD (Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: The number of cells in the SAM slightly increased between 2wSD and 3wSD in wild-type plants grown in non-inductive SDs.
source: During this time, the number of cells in the SAM also slightly increased (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: When 2-week-old SD-grown plants were transferred to LDs, both SAM area and the number of cells in the SAM increased rapidly.
source: By contrast, when 2-week-old SD-grown plants were transferred to LDs, both SAM area and the number of cells in the SAM increased rapidly (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: A dramatic increase in the number of cells in the SAM was observed between 3 and 5 days after transfer to LDs.
source: In particular, a dramatic increase in the number of cells in the SAM was observed between 3 and 5 days after transfer to LDs (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: The increase in cell number was associated with doming of the SAM.
source: This increase in cell number was associated with doming of the SAM (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: Between 5 and 7 days after transfer to LDs, the area of the SAM and the distance between primordia on opposite sides of the SAM decreased.
source: Later, between 5 and 7 days after transfer to LDs, the area of the SAM and the distance between primordia on opposite sides of the SAM decreased, although the number of cells in the SAM did not change significantly between these two time points (Figure 1E and F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: Cell size in the SAM significantly increased between 3 and 5 days after transfer to LDs.
source: Statistical analysis showed that cell size in the SAM significantly increased between 3 and 5 days after transfer to LDs, and decreased again between 5 and 7 LDs (Figure 1D and G).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: Cell size increased in response to LDs in both the central region and the outer ring area of the SAM, but the effect was stronger in the outer ring area.
source: Cell size increased in response to LDs in both regions, but the effect was stronger in the outer ring area than in the central region (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: The number of cells in the SAM was significantly lower in ft-10 tsf-1 mutants exposed to LDs than in wild-type Col-0.
source: Although the size of the SAM of ft-10 tsf-1 was higher in plants transferred to LDs compared to those maintained in SDs, the number of cells in the SAM was significantly lower in ft-10 tsf-1 mutants exposed to LDs than in wild-type Col-0 (Figure 1A–C,E, and F).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: No transient increase in cell size was observed in the ft-10 tsf-1 mutant at five LDs.
source: Besides a small increase in cell size observed at seven LDs, no transient increase in cell size was observed in the ft-10 tsf-1 mutant at five LDs (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: Doming of the SAM was strongly delayed in the ft-10 tsf-1 mutant.
source: Consistent with this observation, doming of the SAM was strongly delayed in this background, although the area of the SAM expanded laterally after transfer to LDs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: Both cell number and meristem size were reduced in KNAT1::GA2ox7 after growth for 2wSD and transfer to 5 and 7 LDs.
source: Both cell number and meristem size were reduced in KNAT1::GA2ox7 after growth for 2wSD and transfer to 5 and 7 LDs, similar to ft-10 tsf-1 (Figure 1A–F).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: The meristem of the KNAT1::GA2ox7 line was morphologically different from that of the ft-10 tsf-1 mutant, with a specific reduction in meristem width.
source: However, the meristem of the KNAT1::GA2ox7 line was morphologically different from that of the ft-10 tsf-1 mutant, with a specific reduction in meristem width (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,D, and E).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: Cell area in the meristematic region of KNAT1::GA2ox7 was larger than for the ft-10 tsf-1 mutant after five LDs.
source: In addition, cell area in the meristematic region of this line was larger than for the ft-10 tsf-1 mutant after five LDs (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: The VENUS-GA20ox2 transgene complemented the late-flowering phenotype of ga20ox2–1 under SDs.
source: The transgene was introduced into the ga20ox2–1 mutant and complemented its late-flowering phenotype under SDs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: The VENUS-GA20ox2 signal was restricted to the abaxial epidermis of leaf primordia in SDs.
source: The VENUS-GA20ox2 signal was restricted to the abaxial epidermis of leaf primordia in SDs, and expanded into the SAM after plants were transferred to LDs (Figure 2A–D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: The VENUS-GA20ox2 signal was detected in the PZ, predominantly in the L1 layer, during floral transition at 3 and 5 days after transfer to LDs.
source: Notably, the VENUS-GA20ox2 signal was detected not only in the RZ but also in the PZ, predominantly in the L1 layer, during floral transition at 3 and 5 days after transfer to LDs (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: VENUS-GA20ox2 expression was reduced in the inflorescence meristem at 7 LDs.
source: After floral transition, VENUS-GA20ox2 expression was reduced again in the inflorescence meristem at 7 LDs (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: The dynamic change in VENUS-GA20ox2 expression was consistent with the levels of GA20ox2 mRNA detected by RT-qPCR in the shoot apex of wild-type plants transferred from SDs to LDs.
source: This dynamic change in VENUS-GA20ox2 expression was consistent with the levels of GA20ox2 mRNA detected by RT-qPCR in the shoot apex of wild-type plants transferred from SDs to LDs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1H) and was also observed in plants that were germinated and grown continuously in LDs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–G), suggesting that it is tightly associated with the developmental transition of the meristem.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: Treatment with paclobutrazol (PAC) increased the signal intensity of VENUS-GA20ox2 at all time points.
source: Treatment with paclobutrazol (PAC), a GA biosynthesis inhibitor, increased the signal intensity of VENUS-GA20ox2 at all time points, although consistently, no expression was detected in the inner domain of the CZ (Figure 2I–L and Figure 2—figure supplement 2I–L).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: After treatment with GA3, the VENUS-GA20ox2 signal was still detected in the PZ of the SAM and was only slightly reduced in signal intensity.
source: Furthermore, after treatment with GA3, the VENUS-GA20ox2 signal was still detected in the PZ of the SAM and was only slightly reduced in signal intensity (Figure 2E–H and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E–H).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: VENUS-GA20ox2 expression was lower in the CZ and higher in the PZ after exposure to three LDs.
source: Consistent with our observation in the longitudinal sections, VENUS-GA20ox2 expression was lower in the CZ and higher in the PZ after exposure to three LDs.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: VENUS-GA20ox2 signal was not evenly distributed in the PZ, but was detected in distinct patches.
source: Notably, VENUS-GA20ox2 signal was not evenly distributed in the PZ, but was detected in distinct patches (Figure 2M).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: The regions that express VENUS-GA20ox2 probably correspond to incipient primordia.
source: Considering the positions of leaf primordia, the regions that express VENUS-GA20ox2 probably correspond to incipient primordia (Figure 2M).
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the study with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: The VENUS-GA20ox2 signal was upregulated after exposure to 3LDs in plants that were still in the vegetative phase.
source: Plants grown under SDs for different time periods were transferred to LDs, and in those plants that were still in the vegetative phase (2wSD, 3wSD, 4wSD, and 5wSD) the VENUS-GA20ox2 signal was upregulated after exposure to 3LDs (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: The VENUS-GA20ox2 signal was induced in the meristem only in the samples transferred to LDs after 2- or 3wSD.
source: Notably, the VENUS-GA20ox2 signal was induced in the meristem only in the samples transferred to LDs after 2- or 3wSD.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: In the 5LD samples, the meristem area was smaller in ga20ox2–1 compared with Col-0.
source: However, in the 5LD samples, the meristem area was smaller in ga20ox2–1 compared with Col-0 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: Analysis of different regions of the meristem at 5LD detected a reduced number of cells and the presence of smaller cells in the ring outside the central region in ga20ox2–1.
source: Analysis of different regions of the meristem, as described previously in Figure 1—figure supplement 2, at 5LD detected a reduced number of cells and the presence of smaller cells in the ring outside the central region (Figure 3B–F).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: Activity of GA20ox2 contributes to the increase in cell size in the PZ at 5LD during floral transition.
source: This suggests that activity of GA20ox2 contributes to the increase in cell size in the PZ at 5LD during floral transition, but the overall effect of ga20ox2–1 on meristematic cell size is weaker than that of KNAT1:GA2ox7 (Figures 1G and 3D), indicating that other enzymes might also participate in increasing GA level at this stage.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data from the study.

claim: The quintuple mutant in which all five C19-GA2ox genes are mutated flowered with significantly fewer rosette leaves than wild-type plants under LDs.
source: Although the contribution of GA to flowering under LDs was smaller than under SDs, the quintuple mutant in which all five C19-GA2ox genes are mutated (ga2ox1–1, ga2ox2–1, ga2ox3–1, ga2ox4–1, and ga2ox6–2) flowered with significantly fewer rosette leaves than wild-type plants under LDs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: The ga2ox2–1 ga2ox4–1 ga2ox6–2 triple mutant and ga2ox4–1 single mutant flowered as early as the ga2ox quintuple mutant.
source: Notably, the ga2ox2–1 ga2ox4–1 ga2ox6–2 triple mutant and ga2ox4–1 single mutant flowered as early as the ga2ox quintuple mutant (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C), suggesting that GA2ox4 is the major enzyme in this class that delays flowering time under LDs.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: GA2ox4 is the major enzyme in the C19-GA2ox class that delays flowering time under LDs.
source: Notably, the ga2ox2–1 ga2ox4–1 ga2ox6–2 triple mutant and ga2ox4–1 single mutant flowered as early as the ga2ox quintuple mutant (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C), suggesting that GA2ox4 is the major enzyme in this class that delays flowering time under LDs.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data from the study.

claim: The number of cauline leaves was indistinguishable in ga2ox mutants and wild-type plants.
source: The number of cauline leaves was indistinguishable in ga2ox mutants and wild-type plants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that C19-GA2ox enzymes increase the duration of vegetative development prior to shoot elongation, but are not involved in regulating the transition from cauline leaves to floral primordia after bolting.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: C19-GA2ox enzymes increase the duration of vegetative development prior to shoot elongation, but are not involved in regulating the transition from cauline leaves to floral primordia after bolting.
source: The number of cauline leaves was indistinguishable in ga2ox mutants and wild-type plants (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that C19-GA2ox enzymes increase the duration of vegetative development prior to shoot elongation, but are not involved in regulating the transition from cauline leaves to floral primordia after bolting.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data from the study.

claim: ga20ox2 mutants possessed more rosette leaves and fewer cauline leaves in LDs.
source: However, ga20ox2 mutants possessed more rosette leaves and fewer cauline leaves in LDs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D), suggesting that in wild-type plants GA20ox2 contributes to the synthesis of GA that promotes transition from the vegetative to inflorescence stage and delays the switch from cauline leaves to floral meristem identity (Yamaguchi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: GA20ox2 contributes to the synthesis of GA that promotes transition from the vegetative to inflorescence stage and delays the switch from cauline leaves to floral meristem identity.
source: However, ga20ox2 mutants possessed more rosette leaves and fewer cauline leaves in LDs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D), suggesting that in wild-type plants GA20ox2 contributes to the synthesis of GA that promotes transition from the vegetative to inflorescence stage and delays the switch from cauline leaves to floral meristem identity (Yamaguchi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data from the study with citation.

claim: After transfer of plants from 3wSDs to LDs, the relatively high level of GA2ox4 mRNA under SDs was downregulated after 3–5 days in LDs, and upregulated again after 7 days in LDs.
source: After transfer of plants from 3wSDs to LDs, the relatively high level of GA2ox4 mRNA under SDs was downregulated after 3–5 days in LDs, and upregulated again after 7 days in LDs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: The dynamic change in GA2ox4 mRNA was almost complementary to that in GA20ox2 expression.
source: This dynamic change in GA2ox4 mRNA was almost complementary to that in GA20ox2 expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: VENUS-GA2ox4 signal was strongly detected in the abaxial side of leaf primordia and in the PZ of the vegetative SAM.
source: By contrast, VENUS-GA2ox4 signal was strongly detected in the abaxial side of leaf primordia and in the PZ of the vegetative SAM, where the future primordia will be initiated (Figure 4A and E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1K, Figure 4—figure supplement 2A, Figure 4—figure supplement 3A and E, and Figure 4—figure supplement 4B–E).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: Three days after transfer of 2wSD-grown plants to LDs, the VENUS-GA2ox4 signal was excluded from the PZ and restricted to the abaxial side of primordia.
source: Three days after transfer of 2wSD-grown plants to LDs, the VENUS-GA2ox4 signal was excluded from the PZ and restricted to the abaxial side of primordia (Figure 4B and F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1L, Figure 4—figure supplement 2B, and Figure 4—figure supplement 3B), and almost disappeared 5 days after transfer (Figure 4C and G, Figure 4—figure supplement 1M, Figure 4—figure supplement 2C, and Figure 4—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: Seven days after transfer to LDs, VENUS-GA2ox4 signal was detected again strongly in floral primordia.

claim: VENUS-GA2ox4 signal was hardly detectable in the young primordia during floral transition at 14 LDs.
